# GaitClass Lab: results

**Status: public.** The analysis repository is public at https://github.com/victorgomezadapty/gaitclass-lab. Generated by `scripts/run_analysis.py` from the local copy of the deposited workbook. Every number below is computed in this project; nothing is copied from the companion paper.

This is a transparent re-analysis of an open table of participant level gait means. It is not a new clinical study and not a replication of the paper's machine learning classifier. Each section says what comes from the deposit, what is inferred, and what this analysis adds.

## 1. Source and provenance

* Deposit title: *Discrete ankle, knee and hip kinematic parameters for overground walking assessed using inertial sensors in patients with various orthopaedic conditions*. "GaitClass" is only the file and project short name.
* Zenodo record https://zenodo.org/records/7598463, version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7598463, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7598462, license id `cc-by-4.0`, open access, one file.
* File `data set GaitClass.xlsx`, 88971 bytes, md5 `806f2df6840f5e65d9a9162226ae7547` (verified before every load).
* Sheet `Dataset`: 206 rows, 28 columns (one fully empty trailing column dropped). Missing cells in the file: 0 (gaps were already imputed by the depositors). Sheet `Parameter definition`: a 28 row codebook.
* Direct identifiers: none (no names, dates, contact data, record numbers or images of people). ID is a sequential study number 1 to 206. Quasi identifiers: age in years, sex, BMI, diagnosis group.
* Ethics as reported in the companion paper: Ethics Committee Northwest Switzerland, EKNZ 2022-01511; signed informed consent; retrospective pooling of earlier projects. No trial registration was found.
* Companion paper (cited only, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0): Dammeyer C, et al. J Orthop Res 2024;42(7):1463 to 1472. https://doi.org/10.1002/jor.25797, PMID 38341759.

## 2. Group codes (inferred mapping)

The codebook says: "Participant group [1 = healthy; 1 = hip osteoarthritis; 2 = knee osteoarthritis; 3 = lumbar spinal stenosis; 4 = cervical spinal stenosis]". Code 1 appears twice and code 0 is never listed, while the file uses codes 0 to 4.

| code | n in file | label used here | n reported (Zenodo, paper) | match |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| 0 | 96 | healthy control | 96 | True |
| 1 | 20 | hip OA | 20 | True |
| 2 | 30 | knee OA | 30 | True |
| 3 | 43 | lumbar stenosis | 43 | True |
| 4 | 17 | cervical stenosis | 17 | True |

**Inferred, not stated:** code 0 = healthy control is inferred because its count (96) equals the number of controls reported on Zenodo and in the paper. Codes 1 to 4 follow the codebook and their counts also match. The codebook itself never says 0 = healthy. See `tables/t03_group_codes_inferred_mapping.csv` and `figures/fig01_group_codes.png`.

## 3. Data quality audit

11 columns carry a flag. 4 raw headers do not match their codebook names and 11 headers carry leading or trailing spaces. Nothing was silently fixed; full table in `tables/t02_data_quality_audit.csv`, figure `figures/fig02_data_quality_audit.png`.

| column | codebook_unit | min | max | flag |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Group | 0-4 | 0.00 | 4.00 | codebook typo |
| Speed | m/s | 0.48 | 1.74 | description error |
| StancePct | seconds | 55.83 | 71.77 | unit mismatch |
| StanceDifference | seconds | -8.56 | 6.15 | unit mismatch |
| KneeMinimum | ° | -0.68 | -0.13 | implausible scale |
| HipMinimum | ° | -23.61 | -0.30 | min/max swap in description |
| AnkleICDifference | ° | -8.20 | 9.28 | header mismatch |
| AnklePlantarflexion1Difference | ° | -4.41 | 6.37 | min/max swap in description |
| AnkleDorsalflexionDifference | ° | -16.70 | 9.92 | min/max swap in description |
| AnklePlantarflexion2Difference | ° | -31.04 | 20.08 | min/max swap in description |
| KneeMinimumDifference | ° | -0.45 | 0.45 | implausible scale |

* **Stance**: unit says seconds, values run 55.83 to 71.77. Assumption used in this project: percent of the gait cycle. The column is renamed `StancePct`; values unchanged.
* **KneeMinimum**: -0.68 to -0.13, against KneeMaximum 3.11 to 34.15 degrees. Scale unknown, so KneeMinimum and its side difference are excluded from contrasts and classifiers and shown only descriptively.
* **HipMinimum**: described as "Global hip maximum", yet the largest value is -0.3 (all negative). Treated as a minimum, as the column name says.
* **Speed**: description reads "Meters"; values fit m/s. **Difference columns**: three ankle descriptions swap minimum and maximum.

## 4. Demographics by group

| group | n | age mean | age SD | age 95% CI low | age 95% CI high | BMI mean | % female |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| healthy control | 96 | 62.5 | 11.8 | 60.1 | 64.9 | 25.0 | 40.6 |
| hip OA | 20 | 61.4 | 11.6 | 56.0 | 66.8 | 28.3 | 55.0 |
| knee OA | 30 | 69.1 | 10.4 | 65.2 | 73.0 | 28.1 | 53.3 |
| lumbar stenosis | 43 | 71.0 | 7.2 | 68.8 | 73.2 | 27.8 | 48.8 |
| cervical stenosis | 17 | 61.4 | 11.0 | 55.8 | 67.1 | 26.6 | 47.1 |

Controls average 62.5 years against 69.1 (knee OA) and 71.0 (lumbar stenosis). Age differs across groups (Kruskal Wallis p <0.001), as does BMI (p <0.001); sex does not (chi square p 0.633). **Controls are not age matched.** Patients were candidates for surgery (advanced disease) or, for cervical stenosis, partly treated conservatively, so results do not describe early disease. Kinematic summaries per group with 95% CIs, medians and IQRs: `tables/t05_features_by_group.csv`.

Model per feature: OLS, feature on group (reference healthy control) plus age and sex, HC3 robust standard errors, Holm correction across the 32 group by feature contrasts. Holm significant contrasts: 19 unadjusted, 18 after age and sex adjustment, 15 when BMI is added, and 15 after removing the 38 rows with imputation footprints.
Lost after age and sex adjustment: AnkleDorsalflexion (lumbar stenosis). Gained: none. Lost after removing flagged rows: KneeIC (cervical stenosis), StancePct (cervical stenosis), StancePct (knee OA).

Reading guide: angles are sagittal plane degrees as deposited (flexion positive). Std diff is the adjusted difference divided by the control SD. Units: Speed m/s, StancePct % of gait cycle (assumed). Caution for hip features: the deposit reports the "affected" side; per the paper, in controls and stenosis groups that side was chosen as the side with less hip flexion, while in hip and knee OA it is the clinical side. Hip contrasts therefore partly reflect a selection rule, not only disease. Age slopes per 10 years: `tables/t07_age_effect_per_10_years.csv`. Forest plot: `figures/fig04_adjusted_contrasts.png`.

## 6. Imputation footprints and leakage

The deposit states that gaps were filled with the control group mean (controls) and by nearest neighbours (patients), but imputed cells are not flagged and the file has no missing values left, so **the original missingness cannot be recovered**. This project detects footprints instead: a value stored with about 15 decimals that appears in two or more rows cannot be an independent measurement, and an exact 0.0 side difference means both sides are identical. This is a lower bound: a cell imputed only once in its column leaves no trace.

| group | n | rows flagged | % rows flagged | suspected cells |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| healthy control | 96 | 27 | 28.1 | 66 |
| hip OA | 20 | 3 | 15.0 | 11 |
| knee OA | 30 | 5 | 16.7 | 8 |
| lumbar stenosis | 43 | 3 | 7.0 | 10 |
| cervical stenosis | 17 | 0 | 0.0 | 0 |

* 95 suspected cells in 38 rows. Controls: 27/96 rows flagged; patients: 11/110 (odds ratio 3.52, Fisher p 0.001). The fill rule and the amount of filling both depend on the label.
* Largest shared value: one `AnklePlantarflexion2` value repeated in 19 rows (15 CTRL, 4 KOA). Four knee OA rows carry the same constant as 15 controls, which does not match the stated patient rule (nearest neighbours); the reason cannot be checked from the file.
* Several control pairs share a whole knee and hip block, which looks like nearest neighbour copying in controls too. Full list: `tables/t08_shared_values_imputation_footprints.csv`.
* Constant fills shrink the control spread: in `AnklePlantarflexion2` the control SD is 6.38 with all rows and 6.94 without suspected cells (`tables/t10_control_spread_shrinkage.csv`).

**Leakage sensitivity analysis (healthy vs patient).** This is not a diagnostic model and does not replicate or compete with the paper's classifier (different software, features, preprocessing and splits). Logistic regression with standardisation, stratified 5 fold cross validation repeated 20 times; cluster aware runs keep rows that share an imputed value in the same fold. AUC mean (2.5 to 97.5 percentile across repeats):

| scenario | rows | AUC mean | AUC p2.5 | AUC p97.5 | balanced accuracy |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| A. demographics only (age, sex, BMI) | 206 | 0.699 | 0.688 | 0.713 | 0.672 |
| B. imputation flag only (no gait, no demographics) | 206 | 0.557 | 0.545 | 0.571 | 0.591 |
| C. gait features, standard CV | 206 | 0.777 | 0.742 | 0.803 | 0.720 |
| D. gait features, cluster-aware CV | 206 | 0.768 | 0.750 | 0.800 | 0.711 |
| E. gait features, flagged rows removed | 168 | 0.757 | 0.729 | 0.779 | 0.700 |
| F. gait + demographics, standard CV | 206 | 0.765 | 0.737 | 0.790 | 0.710 |
| G. gait + demographics, flagged rows removed | 168 | 0.774 | 0.746 | 0.797 | 0.721 |
| H. 1-NN on gait features, standard CV | 206 | 0.621 | 0.598 | 0.641 | 0.621 |
| I. 1-NN on gait features, cluster-aware CV | 206 | 0.616 | 0.592 | 0.651 | 0.616 |

* The imputation flag alone, with no gait or demographic data, separates controls from patients above chance: AUC 0.557 (0.545 to 0.571). That is label information carried by the cleaning process, not by gait.
* Demographics alone give AUC 0.699 (0.688 to 0.713), so part of any separation is age and BMI, not gait.
* Gait features: 0.777 (0.742 to 0.803) with standard CV, 0.768 (0.750 to 0.800) with cluster aware CV and 0.757 (0.729 to 0.779) with flagged rows removed (168 rows, so not a like for like comparison). Detectable footprints do not measurably inflate gait based AUC here; the clearest leakage signal is the flag only result above. Imputations that left no footprint remain a risk that cannot be quantified from this file.

## 7. What cannot be replicated from the deposit

* No raw IMU signals or gait cycles: only per participant means of discrete parameters.
* No outcomes, PROMs, disease severity, side of disease or surgery data.
* The affected side rule for controls and stenosis groups is described only in the paper.
* Zenodo says about 30 steps per participant; the paper reports a median of 13 steps per trial.
* Participant flow: 254 in the earlier projects (Zenodo: extracted; paper: collected), 236 met inclusion per the paper, 206 analysed. The file holds the 206 only, so exclusions cannot be checked.
* Which cells were imputed, and the paper's train and test splits.
* Therefore the paper's classifier accuracies are not reproduced or compared here.

## 8. What this re-analysis adds

1. A column by column audit: 11 flagged columns, including the Stance unit (55.83 to 71.77, read as % gait cycle) and the KneeMinimum scale (-0.68 to -0.13).
2. An explicit, labelled inference for the group codes (0 = healthy control) checked against reported sizes.
3. Age and sex adjusted contrasts for 8 pre-specified features with robust CIs and Holm correction: 18 of 32 contrasts hold after adjustment (unadjusted 19).
4. An imputation leakage check: 38 rows with footprints, controls flagged more often (OR 3.52), flag alone AUC 0.557.

## 9. Limitations

Retrospective data pooled from earlier projects of one hospital research group (University Hospital Basel) and one IMU system, sagittal plane only, small and unequal groups (17 to 96), controls younger and leaner, advanced disease only, imputed values that cannot be fully identified, codebook errors resolved by stated assumptions, and a side selection rule that differs by group. Associations only; not clinical advice.
